title.en: France evacuates 20,000 as wildfires spread in south-west
title.zh: 法国大火致数千人撤离

summary.en: Wildfires continue to rage across Europe, leading to the evacuation of thousands of people. Tragically, a third firefighter has died while battling these blazes.
summary.zh: 欧洲各地野火持续肆虐，导致数千人撤离。不幸的是，在扑救这些大火的过程中，第三名消防员殉职。

body.en:
About 12,000 people have been evacuated from the south-west of France and authorities are moving 8,800 others as wildfires spread in the Gironde region, the local prefect has said.

Sophie Brocas told reporters 2,400 hectares (5,900 acres) of land had already been destroyed around the Bay of Arcachon.

Many of those who had to leave the area overnight were visitors to local campsites on the Lège-Cap-Ferret peninsula and the latest evacuations also involved campsites as a precaution.

Wildfires have also broken out in Spain and Italy in recent days. Residents were evacuated near Toledo south of Madrid and a firefighter died after falling ill while tackling a blaze in Sicily.

The Gironde prefect said 10,000 visitors were among those evacuated from campsites overnight and the latest evacuations were going ahead "calmly" in the village of Claouey, on the shore of Arcachon Bay.

Brocas said no injuries had been reported. Some sites and roads were being closed in exposed forest areas.

"The work was relentless all night," said Gironde fire service chief Marc Vermeulen, who warned that temperatures were rising and the wind was getting stronger. "It'll peak at 20:00. Then we'll have to deal with... highly variable winds so we're currently tackling a fire that is going to be difficult to predict and that's why we cannot relax our guard."

Two local firefighters died earlier this week fighting another fire close to Bordeaux airport.

Yassmina de Freitas, 19, who lives in the coastal town of Le Porge, said she noticed smoke and the smell of burning at lunchtime on Wednesday.

By the afternoon "ash… [and] half-burned tree bark" were falling, the sky was "very dark" and the smoke was getting "thicker and thicker".

At around 20:00 local time (19:00 BST), her family was evacuated by law enforcement and taken to a gymnasium in a neighbouring town. They had to leave two of their cats and four chickens behind as they could not be found in the flurry to leave.

She said she could not sleep at all and was waking up every hour to check the fire's progress.

BBC South presenter Jo Kent is on holiday with her family in France, staying at the Lesley Pastourelles campsite in the village of Claouey, next to Lège.

She said multiple people at the campsite who were very anxious about the situation had already left, and those staying have been warned to be prepared to evacuate.

The main road down to the south of the peninsula, which is normally filled with "nose to tail traffic", is empty and the supermarket is "unnervingly quiet", Kent added.

body.en: Conflict continues across the region as White House announces nuclear technology agreement. Plus, the artist who flattened a Tesla with a tank Good morning. The US has signed a landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that could allow the kingdom to enrich uranium in the future. The deal will be submitted to Congress for review, where it could face opposition among lawmakers who fear a lack of monitoring safeguards. In lengthy talks stretching over more than one administration, the US has feared that Riyadh would look elsewhere for nuclear technology if the US did not provide what it wanted. Saudi Arabia has long said that if it does not partner with the US, it could do so with China or Russia, which have different proliferation standards. Why is a uranium deal with Saudi Arabia controversial? The full details of the deal have yet to be released, but it comes as the US’s war with Iran is being fought in part to prevent Tehran enriching uranium domestically and make it near impossible for Iran to build a nuclear weapon. Saudi Arabia has in the past said it would need a nuclear weapon if Iran acquired one. Kenneth Roth has analysed why Trump would agree it right now . What are the latest developments in the war? The US military launched its 12th successive night of strikes , which have now widened to western and central Iran. In attacks lasting five hours, the US claims to have struck military targets including maritime capabilities, missile and ⁠drone storage facilities, coastal surveillance sites and air defense assets. Yemen’s ⁠Houthi militia also attacked two ​Saudi Arabian oil tankers, the Iran-aligned group said on Thursday, with a Saudi news agency later confirming one of the vessels was ablaze in the Red Sea. title.en: 'Let's enjoy the ride' says Elon Musk, as AI fears mount
title.zh: 随着人工智能的恐惧加剧，埃隆·马斯克说：“让我们享受这段旅程吧”

summary.en: Talking to The Economist, Musk said he doesn't care if people hate him and said he was not a racist.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As AI continues to evolve at breakneck speed, and developers warn of models going rogue, Elon Musk says people should simply "enjoy the ride".

The boss of SpaceX told The Economist , external while he remains concerned about risks posed by advancements in AI and robotics, "the most likely outcome is incredible abundance for all".

Musk said his "philosophical conclusion" after fearing for AI's threat to humanity was to "look on the bright side". He said progress has come so quickly "even if I wanted to stop it, I couldn't".

The interview was recorded the day before OpenAI's revelation on Tuesday that some of its most advanced AI models hacked a start-up after it lost control of them during a security test .

It sparked concerns about AI systems falling out of alignment with human values, though some have pointed out OpenAI - which is seeking to float on the stock market - has an interest in talking up the power of its tools.

The Economist's editor-in-chief Zanny Minton Beddoes questioned Musk on a range of topics, from whether he believed big tech executives should work together to tackle AI safety risks to why he intervenes in European politics.

With the rise of rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic, Musk said: "It just seems like all roads lead to acceleration of AI... you can just sort of be sad about it or join the club, I suppose."

In a wide-ranging interview, the entrepreneur also made typically outlandish predictions, such as claiming "money won't matter" in a decade.

Minton Beddoes said both data and her own experience of living in the UK told a different story to the image portrayed by the trillionaire in his X posts.

"You come see my country that I live in all the time," she said when Musk offered to take her on a tour of the country.

The trillionaire was also asked about his sharing of a film on X reportedly banned in Germany for its violence and anti-migrant message , external .

"My partner is... she's half Indian, and I have four children with her," Musk said of his partner Shivon Zillis, an executive at his brain tech firm Neuralink.

"One of them was named after a famous Indian physicist, so I would say I'm not racist."

Musk also said there were "senior executives of all races" at his companies, adding: "I don't think there's any racism there".

"If people are coming to a country with antithetical views, I am against that," he said.

"I'm against rape and murder, I'm against the imposition of rules and laws that are contrary to what we've come to accept in the West," he continued, criticising the media for not understanding or reflecting this.

title.en: Trump's nuclear deal with Saudis jettisons longstanding US demands

summary.en: Past US presidents insisted that Saudi Arabia normalise relations with Israel in exchange for nuclear technology.

body.en:
The Trump administration's nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia reversed a years-long stance toward a key Middle East ally.

Past US presidents insisted that Saudi Arabia normalise relations with Israel in exchange for receiving American nuclear technology for civilian energy programmes.

President Donald Trump gave Saudi Arabia what it wanted without extracting concessions for Israel in return - and over objections from critics who argued that it could spark a nuclear arms race in the region.

The deal was the latest example of Trump jettisoning the traditional American approach to the Middle East, which centred on Israel and finding a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

In his second term Trump has focused primarily on strengthening America's economic influence to compete with China and other rivals. Analysts said the nuclear pact with Saudi Arabia sent a signal that the US wants to keep regional allies in the fold even if it means angering Israel in the process.

"Countries in the Middle East want to develop their nuclear infrastructure and they're going to do it even if the US is not involved. Washington at this point is recognising that," said Yusuf Can, a Middle East expert at consulting firm Amena Strategies. With this nuclear deal, he added, "the US is basically saying you don't have to work with China. You can work with us".

Transactional foreign policy has been a hallmark of Trump's second term. The US has ratcheted up economic competition with adversaries like China and Russia in the Arctic and other parts of the world since Trump returned to office vowing to revive his "America First" approach to global affairs.

But signing a nuclear pact in the Middle East is an especially bold move that will raise tensions in a volatile region where the US is at war with Iran.

It represents a major victory for Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who has sought a nuclear agreement with the US for years as part of a broader campaign to strengthen relations with the West.

The crown prince, known as MBS, said in 2018 that if Iran develops nuclear weapons then Saudi Arabia should be allowed to as well.

Details of the deal were not immediately released by the administration, but the pact reportedly does not include strict enforcement measures to block Saudi Arabia from developing a military nuclear programme in the future.

In that respect it differs from a 2009 nuclear cooperation agreement struck by the US and the United Arab Emirates which included strict inspections by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Another key difference that critics of the Saudi deal are pointing to is that it reportedly allows them to enrich uranium themselves on their own soil.

title.en: EU fines Google €890 million over competition rules
title.zh: 欧盟因违反竞争规则对谷歌处以8.9亿欧元罚款

summary.en: The European Commission has imposed a fine of €890 million on Google, stating that the tech giant unfairly favored its own search engine and app store, thereby harming competition.
summary.zh: 欧盟委员会对谷歌处以8.9亿欧元罚款，称这家科技巨头通过不公平地偏袒其自身的搜索引擎和应用商店，损害了市场竞争。

body.en:
The European Commission said it found that Google had preferenced its search engine and app store in ways that unfairly harmed competition.

The European Union has imposed fines of €890 million ($1.015 billion) on US tech giant Google for violating EU digital regulations.

The European Commission said it found that Google had preferenced its ubiquitious search engine and its Play app store in ways that unfairly harmed competition.

"We found that Google harms businesses offering similar services, such as shopping or sports, by not granting them the same level of prominence on Google Search," Digital Commissioner Henna Virkkunen said.

"We also found that Google has restricted app developers from offering cheaper offers to customers in the Google Play app store," she said.

The commission stressed that Google could face further fines if it does not take steps to comply with regulations.

"The best products should succeed because they’re better, not because they’re owned by the company running the search engine," Competition Commissioner Teresa Ribera said. "European consumers have a right to be told by app developers where to sign up to the best offers, even when the app store owner does not get a cut."

The EU has described Google and its parent company Alphabet as a "gatekeeper" alongside other major US firms — namely Amazon, Apple, Meta and Microsft — and China's ByteDance, saying that the companies control access for consumers. 

Top Google executive Kent Walker criticized the fine, describing it as "product degradation driven by a small group of self-serving complainants."

He said that the penalty would "strip away real-time search features Europeans love — like instant pricing and direct availability for hotels, flights, and restaurants — and dismantle safety protections on Google Play."

The European Union has been working to rein in Big Tech companies in the face of larget market shares held by major US and Chinese firms.

The European Commission already imposed a €4.3 billion penalty on Google in 2018 , accusing the company of abusing Android system's market dominance by requiring phone makers to pre-install Google Search and the Google Chrome web browser. The firm lost its appeal against the fine in February.

The EU has also fined tech firms under safety regulations, with  Chinese retailer Ali Express being hit with a €550 million fine earlier this month after the bloc had found shortcomings in the firm's efforts to curb illegal, unsafe and counterfeit goods.

On July 10, the EU threatened social media giant Meta with a heavy fine unless it changes "addictive design" used on the platforms Facebook and Instagram.

title.en: Could Iran become America's next 'forever war'?
title.zh: 伊朗会成为美国的下一场“永远的战争”吗？

summary.en: The ceasefire has collapsed, attacks are escalating and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz remains under threat. Is the US drifting into another open-ended conflict with no clear way out?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The ceasefire has collapsed, attacks are escalating and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz remains under threat. Is the US drifting into another open-ended conflict with no clear way out?

As the United States and Iran  exchange ever more powerful strikes, the June truce now is effectively dead. Air raids, drone attacks and missile launches have again become a daily feature of the conflict. The question is no longer whether Washington and Tehran are back at war , but whether the conflict is turning into an open-ended struggle that neither side can win.

The war could indeed become another "forever war," said Kelly Grieco, a senior fellow with the Reimagining US Grand Strategy Program at the Stimson Center, a Washington-based think tank. The term describes conflicts that drag on for years, with repeated military action and no lasting political settlement. "You end up in this 'mow the lawn' approach, where Iranian capabilities grow up to some level. You decide that you're not willing to tolerate that level of threat, and you come back and you do another round of missile strikes and bombings. And then we repeat this cycle endlessly."

US warplanes have intensified their strikes against targets across Iran, while Tehran continues to attack US positions and regional allies . Iranian forces targeted sites in several Gulf countries and again disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz , through which roughly a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas once passed. At the same time, Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen threatened Saudi Arabia's maritime trade routes , raising fears that a second strategic chokepoint could be drawn into the conflict.

Diplomatic efforts have not stopped. Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni traveled to Pakistan, one of the key mediators behind last month's ceasefire agreement, in an attempt to revive talks. But prospects for a breakthrough appear slim. While US President Donald Trump has at times expressed interest in talks with Tehran, he voiced little enthusiasm for new negotiations, saying on Tuesday that the US had "no interest in meeting." He signaled that the US air campaign could intensify further, while Iranian officials have warned that attacks on nuclear sites could trigger another major escalation.

What began as a limited military campaign could evolve into a war of attrition, fought through air strikes, economic pressure and recurring escalations, with no clear end in sight.

title.en: South Korea woman acquitted of murdering newborn after hospital delivery
title.zh: 韩国妇女在医院分娩后谋杀新生儿被判无罪

summary.en: The woman, who had wanted to end her pregnancy at 36 weeks, gave birth to a baby who doctors later killed.

body.en:
A South Korean court has acquitted a woman previously convicted of murdering a baby she delivered in hospital - the latest twist in a case that has gripped the country and fuelled debate about its murky abortion laws.

The woman had wanted to terminate her pregnancy at 36 weeks, but prosecutors said the baby was born alive and later killed.

The woman, identified only by her surname Kwon, was convicted of murder alongside two doctors in March. She was given a three-year suspended jail sentence.

While the doctors' murder convictions were upheld, the appeals court reduced their jail sentences.

The surgeon who operated on Kwon had his sentence reduced from four years to two-and-a-half years. The hospital's director, initially sentenced to six years in prison, had his jail term reduced to four.

This case came to light in 2024 after Kwon, who was in her 20s, posted a YouTube video about terminating her pregnancy at 36 weeks - just over eight months.

The video triggered public uproar and a criminal complaint from the health ministry. Police then launched an investigation into her and her doctors.

The trial against Kwon and her doctors marked the first time that murder charges had been pressed against a woman seeking late-stage termination of their pregnancy, as well as the doctors involved in the procedure.

While abortions were decriminalised in South Korea 2019, there is no clear regulation on how far into pregnancy it can be carried out.

Prosecutors in Kwon's case said the baby was born alive through a Caesarean section and placed in a freezer until it died. The hospital staff then falsified Kwon's medical records to make it look like she had a stillbirth, prosecutors said.

Kwon's lawyer argued that she did not know the baby would be killed after being removed from her womb. This was also the argument that her appeal hinged on.

The judge who gave the initial verdict in March ruled that Kwon had known the baby would be born alive through Caesarean section.

But on Thursday, the appeals court ruled that this might not have been the case, as a broker had told Kwon the baby would be stillborn.

Heekyoung Cho, Amnesty International Korea's executive director, said in a statement that the group welcomed the court's decision to acquit Kwon, but added that the void in South Korea's abortion law has "left pregnant people without clear legal protections and access to essential reproductive healthcare".

"The government must implement measures to remove barriers to accessing safe abortion as well as to provide proper regulations on abortion service provision," she said.

body.zh: 韩国一家法院宣判一名因谋杀医院产下婴儿而被定罪的妇女无罪，这是该国关注的案件的最新转折，并引发了有关其模糊堕胎法的争论。 这名妇女原本想在怀孕36周时终止妊娠，但检察官表示，孩子生下来时还活着，后来被杀死了。 这名女子姓权，三月份与两名医生一起被判犯有谋杀罪。她被判处三年缓刑。 虽然维持了医生的谋杀罪，但上诉法院减轻了他们的刑期。 为权进行手术的外科医生的刑期从四年减至两年半。该医院院长最初被判处六年监禁，现已减为四年。 此案于 2024 年曝光，当时 20 多岁的 Kwon 在 YouTube 上发布了一段关于在 36 周（仅 8 个多月）时终止妊娠的视频。 该视频引发公众轩然大波，并引起卫生部的刑事投诉。警方随后对她和她的医生展开调查。 对权及其医生的审判标志着首次对寻求晚期终止妊娠的妇女以及参与该手术的医生提出谋杀指控。 虽然韩国 2019 年将堕胎合法化，但对于怀孕多久可以进行堕胎并没有明确的规定。 权案的检察官表示，这名婴儿是通过剖腹产活产的，并被放在冰箱里直到死亡。检察官称，医院工作人员随后伪造了权的医疗记录，使她看起来像是死产。 权的律师辩称，她不知道婴儿从子宫中取出后会被杀死。这也是她上诉所依据的论点。 三月份做出初步判决的法官裁定，权某知道婴儿会通过剖腹产活产。 但周四，上诉法院裁定情况可能并非如此，因为一名经纪人告诉权，婴儿将是死产。 国际特赦组织韩国执行主任赵熙瑛在一份声明中表示，该组织对法院宣判权无罪的决定表示欢迎，但他补充说，韩国堕胎法的空白“导致孕妇得不到明确的法律保护，无法获得基本的生殖保健”​​。 “政府必须采取措施消除安全堕胎的障碍，并对堕胎服务提供适当的监管，”她说。 在审判的早些时候，权告诉法庭，她在七个月后才得知自己怀孕，并寻求堕胎，因为她没有稳定的收入。她还担心孩子会...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 随着中国模式的普及，中美人工智能竞争加剧

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

title.en: US signs landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
title.zh: 美国与沙特阿拉伯签署具有里程碑意义的核协议

summary.en: The US Department of Energy says the "peaceful" co-operation agreement will give US firms "great access" to the Saudi nuclear energy programme.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US and Saudi Arabia have signed a landmark deal that will allow the Gulf kingdom to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

The deal is described as a "peaceful nuclear co-operation agreement" that will provide "great access for American companies in the Saudi nuclear energy program" by the US energy department.

Text from the deal has not been made public, but US media report that it could allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium in the future - which can be used as fuel for power plants, but also to make nuclear bombs.

Experts say that would mark a first for the US and could run the risk of future nuclear proliferation in an already unstable region.

The US Department of Energy said a "bilateral safeguards agreement" had been signed along with the co-operation deal.

"Together, these two agreements lay the legal foundation for a decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership that advances several priority economic and strategic objectives, including nuclear nonproliferation," the statement said.

The Saudi government also released a statement saying the deal "represents an extension of existing co-operation between the two countries in the energy sector", noting that it comes after the Saudi leader visited Washington last November.

The nuclear issue has been at the centre of the months-long US-Israeli conflict with Iran. The two nations say one of the reasons they attacked Iran in February was to prevent the country from ever developing a nuclear weapon - something that Tehran denies planning to do.

Saudi Arabia's de facto ruler, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, told CBS News in 2018 that his own nation was not planning to acquire a nuclear weapon, but that "without a doubt if Iran developed a nuclear bomb, we will follow suit as soon as possible".

Wednesday's announcement came as fighting escalates between the US and Iran. Saudi Arabia, a longtime US ally, hosts several US bases that have been targeted by Iranian attacks. It also comes two days after Iran's allies in Yemen, the Houthis, announced a "maritime blockade" against the kingdom.

Specific details of the nuclear deal have not been given but earlier media reports , external suggested that, after undertaking a joint study with the US, Saudi Arabia may be allowed to enrich uranium on its soil to produce fuel at a US-built enrichment facility, instead of relying on imported fuel.

This could be worth billions of dollars to the US, whose companies could be involved in building a facility to produce enriched uranium, which can be used as fuel for power plants but also to make nuclear bombs.

title.en: Who is Ukraine's new military chief?
title.zh: 乌克兰新任军事指挥官是谁？

summary.en: Mykhailo Drapatyi has been appointed as the new commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces, following a cabinet reshuffle that included the removal of defense minister Fedorov.
summary.zh: 米哈伊洛·德拉帕蒂已被任命为乌克兰武装部队总司令。此次任命是在内阁改组之后进行的，改组中包括国防部长费多罗夫被免职。

body.en:
Mykhailo Drapatyi has been made commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces. His appointment follows a cabinet reshuffle that ousted defense minister Fedorov.

On Tuesday (July 21), Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy appointed Mykhailo Drapatyi as the new commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Zelenskyy wants him to develop a modern defense strategy and to continue the recently launched military reforms.  

This comes after an unexpected cabinet reshuffle last week. Many ministers have retained their posts under new Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi , but not former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who had a major argument with former commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi about the strategic direction that  Ukraine's war effort should take.

The firing of the popular defense minister sparked outrage among parts of Ukraine's population. During mass protests, demonstrators not only demanded his return but also the dismissal of Syrskyi.

While the latter has now been removed from his post, Federov will not be returning. Zelenskyy has appointed Yevhen Khmara, who was previously head of Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), as the new defense minister. 

Mykhailo Drapatyi was the only general who publicly defended Fedorov after his dismissal. He wrote on Facebook that Fedorov's appointment to the defense ministry six months ago had been "a serious attempt to change conditions in the military system that were in place for years."

He added that the Defense Ministry had developed into a true partner for the army: "Cooperation between the troops and the Defense Ministry changed. There was a new willingness to listen to commanders, to take decisions more quickly and to support changes that came from the units themselves."

Drapatyj explained that many of the changes had had to be pushed through despite fierce resistance from the old system, and that there was a need to discuss problems in the army openly and honestly.

Mykhailo Drapatyi (born in 1982) is a highly decorated Ukrainian major general who has distinguished himself as a battle-hardened frontline commander since 2014. At the beginning of the Donbas War, the trained tank trooper became known for his resolve during what was then called an "anti-terror operation."

After Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, he coordinated — as deputy commander of the Ukrainian Joint Forces — the successful defense of the town of Kryvyi Rih as well as the liberation of strategically important areas in the south of the country.

summary.en: The news reports that Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is facing growing political strains and internal unrest, highlighted by a recent military shake-up, as the war against Russia continues.

body.en:
Nearly four and a half years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of his country, Ukrainian President Volodymr Zelenskyy faces one of his toughest domestic political challenges yet.

In the past week, the biggest protests Zelenskyy's leadership has ever seen swept through Kyiv as frustrations over how to win the war against their eastern neighbour spilled over. Thousands of young people took to the streets to protest contentious recruitment methods and decry the allegations of corruption swirling around the administration.

In an effort to placate the demonstrators, Zelenskyy replaced his army chief Oleksandr Syrsky on Wednesday. The 60-year-old veteran commander had been the focus of the unrest following the removal of a younger, reform-minded defence minister.

That minister, 35-year-old Mykhailo Fedorov , was demoted by Zelenskyy just six months into the job. It has been reported that Syrsky may have encouraged Zelenskyy to get rid of the tech-savvy junior and has now himself been replaced by Mykhailo Drapatyi as head of the military.

Some believe that shift suggests Zelenskyy's leadership could be in trouble, especially given it comes after former prime minister Yulia Svyrydenko was replaced earlier this month.

Ukrainian opposition MP Oleksiy Goncharenko told  the SBS World News Weekly podcast  that Zelenskyy's position is "very weakened" amid ongoing corruption scandals, and the rotation of political appointments suggests Zelenskyy is trying to shore up his position.

However, Iryna Skubii, senior researcher in Ukrainian studies at the University of Melbourne, told SBS News that what may appear to be a crisis from the outside reflects "how democracy works" in Ukraine.

"It's how civil society illustrates what they want from political leadership at this time, and political leadership listened to them and made this decision accordingly," she said.

Ukraine has been subject to Russian aggression since the illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014. The conflict escalated when Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Skubii said Ukrainians are understandably tired but remain resolute in their rejection of Russian domination.

Peter Tesch, a former Australian ambassador to Russia, told SBS News that the divide between Syrsky and Fedorov — who is reportedly being considered for another position in Zelenskyy's government — is one between the old guard and the new. title.en: 'Literally terrifying': Does this 'rogue' experiment offer a glimpse of our future?
title.zh: “简直可怕”：这个“流氓”实验是否让我们看到了未来？

summary.en: An autonomous AI agent escaped its testing environment and hacked another technology platform during internal capability experiments.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An AI agent powered by OpenAI broke free of its testing environment and hacked a real-life company, in an incident experts said shows the "magnitude" of the cybersecurity threat posed by artificial intelligence.

The incident, announced by the tech company in a statement on its website on Wednesday, saw a combination of OpenAI models launch a cyber attack on a separate tech platform, Hugging Face, during an internal test of OpenAI's capabilities.

Professor Geoff Webb, Australian laureate fellow in the department of data science and artificial intelligence at Monash University, told SBS News it was "literally terrifying" to consider what the same systems could do in the hands of a "malicious actor".

"It shows the magnitude of the task we have in protecting ourselves from these systems in the future," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The news comes after two recent incidents that showed Australia's vulnerability to cyber attacks: when millions of Australians had their data accessed in an Origin Energy hack, and thousands of Australian medical records were accessed in the Partnered Health hack.

Toby Walsh, laureate fellow and professor of artificial intelligence at the University of New South Wales' department of computer science and engineering, said the developments were "troubling".

"All of these models now have pretty strong cyber-capabilities, both for uncovering flaws, bugs that we can then fix, but also in the wrong hands, to exploit those bugs," he told SBS News.

"At the moment, we're relying on the goodwill of OpenAI to tell us what's happening ... We need tougher controls and oversight."

The saga started when Hugging Face, an AI platform for building and sharing machine learning tools, spotted an intrusion from an autonomous AI agent system, writing on their website the attack was "different from anything we had handled before".

OpenAI then announced their models were responsible for the intrusion, after they detected a zero-day flaw in Hugging Face's online security.

"Zero-day flaw means it's a foundational flaw that needs to be fixed now, instantly. You don't wait," Walsh said.

Webb told SBS News the problem with the incident isn't that OpenAI went 'rogue'.

"It wasn't that it decided to do [the attack] anyway. It was told to do it, and it did it. It has now got the capability of figuring it out."

The problem, he said, was that "OpenAI thought they'd put it inside a box it couldn't escape from".

The incident isn't the first to demonstrate the cybersecurity threat of AI. Anthropic temporarily restricted its Claude Mythos model in May after it found more than 10,000 security vulnerabilities in critical software.

title.en: A nuclear-sized risk? The US-Saudi deal changing the equation in the Middle East
title.zh: 核风险？美沙协议改变中东格局

summary.en: A landmark agreement has revived longstanding concerns, and raised fresh questions about the Middle East's nuclear future.
summary.zh: 一项具有里程碑意义的协议重新引发了人们长期以来的担忧，并对中东的核未来提出了新的疑问。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has signed a landmark agreement with Saudi Arabia that will allow the kingdom to build reactors using American technology and to enrich uranium.

The deal, signed on Thursday, is expected to last 30 years and will allow US companies to run commercial power plants in Saudi Arabia.

But experts are concerned the move could open the door for nuclear proliferation — which refers to both the spread of nuclear weapons to more countries and the advancement or stockpiling of nuclear weapons — despite assurances from the US that adequate safeguards are in place.

The agreement comes amid the backdrop of the US' war with Iran, where the US has expressed concern over Iran's nuclear program — an issue that remains a key point of contention during now-stalled peace talks.

Two agreements were signed — one on "peaceful nuclear cooperation", known as a 123 agreement, and another on "bilateral safeguards".

The text of the deals was not immediately made public, except for a statement by the US energy department.

"US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and Saudi Minister of Energy His Royal Highness (HRH) Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman signed a peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement, commonly known as a 123 agreement, alongside an accompanying bilateral safeguards agreement," the announcement read.

"Together, these two agreements lay the legal foundation for a decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership that advances several priority economic and strategic objectives, including nuclear nonproliferation."

The department said the deal would benefit "American industry, workers and supply chains" and help "meet Saudi energy needs".

A key point of concern is that the deal could allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium and reprocess nuclear waste, both of which are potential pathways to making a nuclear weapon.

The United Arab Emirates (UAE) agreed to forgo both of those when it signed a similar deal with the US in 2009.

Discussions of a civil nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia have been in the works for years — under both Trump's first administration and Joe Biden's — but no deal came together before now, in part because of warnings from nonproliferation groups that it could offer Saudi Arabia a path to develop a nuclear weapon.

title.en: Yemen's Houthis claim Red Sea tanker strikes, as Trump threatens Iran's power plants
title.zh: 也门胡塞武装声称袭击红海油轮，特朗普威胁伊朗发电厂

summary.en: Yemen's Houthi group has claimed responsibility for recent tanker strikes in the Red Sea, while former US President Donald Trump has threatened Iranian power plants. These actions are increasing the risk of further disruptions to global oil supplies and prices.

body.en:
Yemen's Houthi rebels have claimed they struck two Saudi Arabian oil tankers in the Red Sea, opening a new front in the US-Iran war engulfing the region and raising the risk of further disruption to global oil trade.

The claim came as the United States launched a fresh wave of strikes on Iranian military targets, marking the twelfth consecutive night of US attacks on Iran.

The Houthis said they had carried out missile and drone strikes on two Saudi tankers that "violated the blockade", naming the vessels as the Encelia and the Layla.

British naval security monitor UKMTO said the master of a tanker reported being struck by an unknown projectile about 70 nautical miles south-west of Al Shuqaiq, causing a fire that the crew was fighting.

The Red Sea escalation followed a Houthi threat to blockade Saudi ports , widening the pressure on key Middle East shipping routes already shaken by fighting over the Strait of Hormuz.

US President Donald Trump had threatened to destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every attack on shipping in Hormuz, drawing an "eye for an eye" warning from Iran as both sides sharpened threats in the escalating war.

Fighting over the vital energy waterway has collapsed a preliminary deal between the US and Iran, with Iran reimposing its blockade and firing on vessels that seek to transit.

"Any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by Missile, Rocket, Drone, or any other device or weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT," Trump wrote on social media.

Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran would respond in kind to any attack on its infrastructure.

"Our defence doctrine is clear: eye for an eye," Araghchi wrote on X. "Any aggression against Iran, including our infrastructure, will compel a powerful and decisive response."

Iran's state broadcaster quoted the military as saying that US threats "will have no result other than the expansion of the war".

Trump has faced intense political pressure to end the conflict, which US defence secretary Pete Hegseth said had cost the United States US$37.5 billion ($53.5 billion), up from nearly US$29 billion ($41.5 billion) in mid-May.

But Trump rejected polls showing the war was unpopular as he headed to an airbase for the return of the remains of four US service personnel.

Three were killed in an Iranian attack on a military base in Jordan, and one died during a controlled detonation of an unexploded Iranian drone in Iraq.

"Americans don't want high gasoline prices but they're not against the war," Trump said.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

title.en: Blocked by censors, China's animal lovers take fight against abuse offline and overseas
title.zh: 遭审查阻挠，中国动物爱好者将反虐待斗争转至线下和海外

summary.en: The killing of a dog and her puppies in Guangdong, China, has provoked widespread outrage both within the country and internationally. Animal welfare advocates, facing censorship, have taken their campaign against animal abuse offline and sought support overseas.
summary.zh: 中国广东省一只狗及其幼崽被杀害的事件，在中国国内外引发了广泛的愤怒。面对审查，动物福利倡导者已将他们的反虐待动物运动转至线下并寻求海外支持。

body.en:
When videos showing the horrific killing of a stray dog and her puppies sparked outrage on the Chinese internet in June, Beijing's censorship machine kicked into action.

But what was unusual this time was that it pitted the shocked and angry voices against authorities who said they were concerned about the four boys involved, all of them younger than 14.

China's Communist Party regime tightly controls media and the internet to suppress criticism of the state and to manage public anger. But in this case authorities cited the age of the boys as they urged people to withhold their comments and scrubbed social media posts about the incident.

"We urge the public not to disseminate related information, to reject cyberbullying, and to work together to create a good environment for the growth of minors," reads an official statement.

But the restrictions only seemed to spur the outcry. China's animal lovers have now taken their fight offline and abroad, even putting up billboards in New York to drum up support.

In China, posts about the incident are still drawing thousands of comments across social media, three weeks after the incident. There is shock, anger and sorrow, as well as demands for laws against animal cruelty, which China currently does not have.

Disturbing footage showing the boys in the city of Jieyang, Guangdong province, hitting three puppies with sticks before setting their mother on fire emerged online at the end of June. The boys were seen laughing as the dog, named Wang Wang, burned.

Jieyang authorities said last month that the boys would not face criminal charges and would instead be sent to a "specialised school", but did not elaborate.

Some reports suggest the boys filmed themselves and uploaded the video online, but police have not commented on that. Censors have tried to block the video to protect the boys' identity, although some people argue that it should stay.

Their identities have not been revealed, but snippets of the video with their faces visible continue to circulate online. There are also unverified posts claiming to be close-ups of the boys' faces, raising the risk of other children being wrongly identified.

Countries around the world restrict information about child offenders or set a high bar for identifying them.

For instance, media coverage and public access to juvenile court documents are often restricted to minimise psychological harm caused by undue publicity.

In this case, Chinese authorities have not completely banned the discussion yet. Keywords such as "Wang Wang" and "animal protection" came up as trending search terms on Monday, but posts related to them started to disappear towards the end of this week. title.en: ‘A statement of freedom’: T-shirt slogan goes viral and book sales rocket in Taiwan after Hong Kong raids

summary.en: Taiwanese citizens express concern over the situation of independent booksellers in Hong Kong following recent arrests. A woman's defiant walk from a bookstore, wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with a "statement of freedom," has gone viral, leading to increased book sales in Taiwan.
summary.zh: 近几个月香港独立书商遭到一系列逮捕后，台湾民众对他们的命运表示担忧。一名女子昂首走出香港一家仅存的独立书店，她T恤上印着的“自由宣言”标语走红，导致台湾的书籍销量飙升。

body.en: Taiwanese people look on with concern at fate of Hong Kong’s independent booksellers, after series of arrests in recent months Walking out of one of Hong Kong’s last remaining independent bookstores, hands behind her back but head held high, the woman’s T-shirt was emblazoned with a simple slogan : “I am a bookstore employee”. Escorted by police, the woman was among five people arrested during raids on two bookstores last week , suspected of displaying and selling publications with “seditious” content, a national security crime which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years. Continue reading...

Yahweh's word reminds us that knowing the truth is intrinsically linked to liberation, offering hope even amidst challenging circumstances. reflection.zh: 在真相被压制之时，寻求和表达真相的简单行为可以成为一种强大的自由宣言。雅伟的话语提醒我们，认识真理与获得自由是紧密相连的，即使在充满挑战的环境中也能带来希望。这个故事凸显了人类对真理及其所带来的自由的持久渴望。

title.en: The Guardian view on Chinese workers picking up the pen: poetry in motion | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》观点：中国工人拿起笔杆子，诗意盎然 | 社论

summary.en: A food delivery rider has won China's highest literary award, highlighting a growing trend of laborers engaging in creative writing. This phenomenon sheds light on the hundreds of millions who have built modern China, from street sweepers to factory workers and goods transporters, revealing their rich inner lives.
summary.zh: 一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖，这凸显了劳动者从事创意写作的日益增长的趋势。这一现象揭示了数亿建设现代中国的劳动者——从扫街工人到工厂员工和货物运输者——丰富的内心世界。

body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. title.en: British woman jailed for blackmail after accusing banker of rape in Hong Kong
title.zh: 英国女子在香港被判勒索罪，此前她指控银行家强奸

summary.en: Isabel Rose was convicted of trying to extort £100,000 from the UK banker and perverting the course of justice.
summary.zh: 伊莎贝尔·罗斯因试图向一名英国银行家勒索10万英镑，并在香港妨碍司法公正而被定罪。

body.en:
A British woman has been jailed for six years in Hong Kong for blackmail and perverting the course of justice after a court found she made a false allegation of rape.

Isabel Rose, 26, from Hackney in east London, alleged that a British banker raped her after she travelled to Hong Kong to visit him in January 2024.

The man was arrested after she reported the incident but later released without charge. Rose was subsequently arrested and charged.

Local media reported that Rose was in Hong Kong's District Court on Wednesday for sentencing after being convicted in March. She had denied the charges.

According to local press reports, Judge Adriana Tse sentenced her to five years in prison for blackmail and three years for perverting the course of justice, with one year to be served consecutively.

Prosecutors argued that Rose fabricated the allegation in an attempt to extort £100,000 ($134,000) from the man, whose identity was withheld. Rose denied the charges throughout the trial and has consistently maintained that she was raped.

Rose had travelled to Hong Kong on 31 January 2024 after meeting the man while in Thailand a month earlier, according to court documents.

At the centre of the prosecution case were WhatsApp messages exchanged between the pair in the hours and days after the alleged rape on 1 February at his apartment.

In one message sent the following morning, Rose wrote: "Are you annoyed I didn't want to have sex," to which the man replied: "What no of course not. Was impressed by your restraint."

Later that day, Rose wrote: "You violated me last night, I didn't wanna have sex."

He replied: "I'm really deeply sorry, I was slightly drunk and I misread your signals, it's no excuse and I know it doesn't make it any better."

In a later exchange, Rose wrote: "You basically raped me." The man replied: "That's not what I'm into at all and I feel sick."

The pair later exchanged messages about money. According to the written judgement of the verdict published in March, the man agreed to reimburse Rose for her travel and accommodation.

In one message, Rose wrote: "Send me the right amount you owe me for everything. Think about that. Think carefully."

Rose subsequently wrote: "You've given 10% of what I'm owed. 100% of my soul gone."

In a later message, the man wrote: "But I don't have 100k, I have no way of paying you that."

Rose reported the rape to police on 3 February. The man was arrested and questioned before being released without charge. Rose was arrested the following day and later charged with blackmail and perverting the course of public justice.

In her verdict, Judge AN Tse Ching relied in part on the messages exchanged after the encounter, according to the South China Morning Post , external .

When the course of justice is perverted, it undermines the very foundation of trust and fairness in society. title.en: Can India become the next semiconductor hub after Taiwan?
title.zh: 印度能否成为继台湾之后的下一个半导体中心？

summary.en: India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.
summary.zh: 随着主要工业强国寻求将供应链多元化，不再只依赖台湾，印度正投入数十亿美元建设国内半导体产业。

body.en:
India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.

More than 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductor chips are made in Taiwan , an island at the center of ongoing rivalry between the US and China .

Any disruption to Taiwan's chip industry would likely send shockwaves through the global economy, with modern semiconductors used to make everything from smartphones and electric vehicles (EVs) to aircraft and military systems .

During the COVID-19 pandemic, chip shortages forced automakers to halt production — exposing how dependent the world had become on a handful of manufacturers in East Asia.

The result has been a global race to build more resilient semiconductor supply chains. The US, Japan, South Korea and also the EU have all launched multi-billion-dollar programs to attract chipmakers.

India is now mounting its biggest push yet to become part of that network and enter the global arena as the next electronics powerhouse.

Last week, the Indian government approved a $13.2 billion (€11.4 billion) semiconductor program labeled Semicon 2.0. The project builds on the $9 billion India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched in 2021 and aims to develop the entire chip ecosystem — from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, specialty materials, equipment manufacturing and workforce training. 

Thousands of engineers working for companies such as Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments already design some of the world's most sophisticated chips from research centers in the Indian cities of Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Noida.

But analysts warn India has been lagging behind in large-scale manufacturing. In the semiconductor industry,  this is the area that brings both economic value and strategic importance.

"India already has the expertise to design sophisticated semiconductor chips," said V Kamakoti, director of the Indian Institute of Technology in the city of Madras.

"Indian engineers working for both domestic companies and multinational firms have successfully designed and delivered complex chips," Kamakoti told DW. "The bigger challenge is manufacturing them."

So far, India's progress has been concentrated in chip packaging and testing rather than manufacturing the chips themselves.

Kamakoti said the next step is building a domestic fabrication ecosystem that can turn those design strengths into large-scale production.

Micron Technology, a US memory chip maker, Kaynes Semicon and CG Semi, two Indian semiconductor assembly and packaging companies, have begun commercial production under the first phase of India's semiconductor program.

reflection.en: Building a new national industry requires immense vision, investment, and diligent effort. As nations embark on such ambitious projects, committing their plans to Yahweh can bring a sense of purpose and trust in the process. This reminds us that all human endeavors, great or small, can be undertaken with a spirit of dependence on divine guidance.
reflection.zh: 建设一个新的国家产业需要巨大的远见、投资和勤奋的努力。当国家着手进行如此宏伟的项目时，将计划交托给雅伟，能带来目标感和对过程的信任。这提醒我们，所有人类的努力，无论大小，都可以在依靠神圣指引的精神下进行。

title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test
title.zh: “强烈关切”：澳大利亚在中国弹道导弹试验后与中方会晤

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

title.en: China narrows AI gap, challenges US influence
title.zh: 中国缩小人工智能差距，挑战美国影响力

summary.en: At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, China showcased its advancements in AI technology and promoted its vision for open-source development and global governance in the field, signaling a challenge to existing international influence.
summary.zh: 在上海举行的世界人工智能大会上，中国展示了其在人工智能技术方面的进展，并推广了其在开源开发和全球治理方面的愿景，这预示着对现有国际影响力的挑战。

body.en:
At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Beijing showcased advances in AI while promoting its vision of open-source development and global governance.

As China narrows the artificial intelligence (AI) gap with the United States,  Beijing is promoting a narrative centered on "open source" and "inclusive AI" as an argument for its vision of global governance.

During his keynote speech at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai on Friday, Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed China's ambition to take a leading role in setting global standards in AI . He criticized what he described as the "overextension of the concept of national security."

Xi did not openly reference the United States. However, Beijing's effort to position itself as an advocate of a new AI order and challenge US dominance was unmistakable.

This year's Shanghai summit sent several important signals, says Rogier Creemers, assistant professor at Leiden University in the Netherlands specializing in China's digital technology policy. The WAIC indicates that artificial intelligence is now one of Beijing's political priorities, and that China intends to compete with the United States by supporting open-source AI models and promoting AI-driven industrialization, Creemers told DW. He also noted China hopes to win support from countries in the Global South for this effort.

China is steadily narrowing the gap with the United States in AI model development, and its efforts at AI application in industrial processes are slowly maturing. 

Chinese AI model developers have continued to keep pace on the global stage, largely by training open-weight models on limited but advanced computer hardware, Paul Triolo, senior vice president for China and tech policy lead at DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group, told DW.

Triolo believes deployment of AI across Chinese enterprises may be progressing faster than in the United States.

In addition, there is less fear of AI among the Chinese population than there is in the US, facilitating more rapid uptake of AI applications at the consumer level.

Earlier this year, Chinese state media claimed that the performance gap between Chinese and US AI models had "largely disappeared."

Several experts broadly agreed with this assessment, saying that certain benchmark tests of China's  large language models (LLMs) such as GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3 showed the gap narrowing or even fully closing.

For most applications, Triolo noted, China's leading open-weight AI models are cheaper to run and more than capable of handling most tasks.

At the same time, advanced proprietary models from leading US companies such as Anthropic, OpenAI  and Google still retain advantages in areas such as...
body.zh: 在上海举行的世界人工智能大会上，北京展示了人工智能的进步，同时宣传其开源发展和全球治理的愿景。 随着中国缩小与美国的人工智能 (AI) 差距，北京正在推动以“开源”和“包容性人工智能”为中心的叙事，作为其全球治理愿景的论据。 中国国家主席习近平周五在上海举行的世界人工智能大会（WAIC）上发表主旨演讲时表达了中国在制定人工智能全球标准方面发挥主导作用的雄心。他批评他所说的“国家安全概念的过度延伸”。 习近平没有公开提及美国。 然而，北京将自己定位为人工智能新秩序倡导者并挑战美国主导地位的努力是明确无误的。 荷兰莱顿大学专门研究中国数字技术政策的助理教授罗吉尔·克里默斯表示，今年的上海峰会发出了几个重要信号。 Creemers 告诉德国之声，WAIC 表明人工智能现在是北京的政治优先事项之一，中国打算通过支持开源人工智能模型和促进人工智能驱动的工业化来与美国竞争。他还指出，中国希望为此赢得南方国家的支持。 中国在人工智能模型开发方面与美国的差距正在稳步缩小，人工智能在工业流程中的应用也正在慢慢成熟。 DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group 中国区高级副总裁兼技术政策负责人 Paul Triolo 告诉德国之声，中国人工智能模型开发人员继续在全球舞台上保持同步，主要是在有限但先进的计算机硬件上训练开放权重模型。 Triolo 认为，中国企业的人工智能部署进展可能比美国更快。 此外，中国民众对人工智能的恐惧程度低于美国民众，这有助于消费者更快速地接受人工智能应用。 今年早些时候，中国官方媒体声称中国和美国人工智能模型之间的性能差距已经“基本消失”。 多位专家普遍同意这一评估，并表示，GLM-5.2和Kimi K3等中国大型语言模型（LLM）的某些基准测试表明，差距正在缩小甚至完全缩小。 Triolo 指出，对于大多数应用程序来说，中国领先的开放式人工智能模型的运行成本更低，并且能够处理大多数任务。 与此同时，Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Google 等美国领先公司的先进专有模型仍然在以下领域保持优势……

Yet, Yahweh's ancient warning from Genesis 11:6 reminds us to consider the spirit behind such endeavors, lest our pursuit of limitless capability overshadow the wisdom of humility and collaboration. title.en: Origin Energy reports customer bank, credit card details caught up in data breach
title.zh: Origin Energy 报告客户银行、信用卡详细信息遭遇数据泄露

summary.en: After advising it had been caught up in a data breach on Wednesday, Origin Energy has revealed the full extent of stolen materials.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A cyberattack on Origin Energy has included unauthorised access and disclosure of customer data, the energy giant says, a day after it revealed it was caught up in the breach.

The Sydney-based company said on Thursday it was working to understand how many of its almost five million customers were affected by the privacy incursion.

Names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and account information could all have been viewed in the breach, Origin said in an ASX statement.

Also at risk were the last four digits of credit cards, or the last three digits of bank accounts.

Origin chief executive Frank Calabria apologised to customers and said the company was working to contact those affected.

The company has set up a contact number and "additional resources to help manage our response to this incident".

"One of our key priorities is taking action to secure our systems and ensure no further unauthorised access," Mr Calabria said.

"We are working with independent cyber experts to support Origin, and that work is continuing alongside the work of authorities."

The company continued to engage with federal cyber and information agencies on the incident as well as police, according to the statement.

Origin, which has 4.8 million customer accounts in Australia and provides electricity, natural gas, LPG and internet services, said on Wednesday it did not believe the data obtained included credit card or bank details.

Griffith University's Graeme Hughes, an expert on business and consumer issues, said the breach was unlikely to cause cases of payment fraud but marked a "social engineering problem".

"The last four digits for a card, a date of birth, and an authentic billing history are the exact trust signals a businesses uses to verify itself over the phone," Professor Hughes told AAP.

"That makes an unsolicited call about an energy account far more convincing than it should be.

"If comparable Australian breaches have taught us anything, the confirmed scope (of the breach) usually widens rather than narrows."

The breach represents the country's most high-profile cyber incident since Partnered Health, owned by private equity firm Quadrant, said earlier in July that its medical records were breached clinics in Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra.

In 2025, airline Qantas said it had customer data published by cybercriminals, while telco giant Optus and health insurer Medibank were hit in attacks in 2022 that sparked cyber-resilience laws.

title.en: Hanson says domestic violence comments taken 'out of context' as criticism mounts

summary.en: The One Nation leader has pinned the blame on media outlets covering comments she made that domestic violence is a "two-way street".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Pauline Hanson has denied downplaying the scourge of domestic violence after labelling the issue a "two-way street", as advocates warn the politician's framing is dangerous.

The One Nation leader is facing criticism from experts over comments she made about domestic violence , which Hanson claimed had been taken out of context by media outlets.

"Domestic violence is wrong, but it's also a two-way street," she told 4BC radio on Wednesday.

"Domestic violence is a scourge, but look ... if you're not in a house where you feel safe ... then you shouldn't put up with it.

"If these women are getting abused by men out there, then don't put up with it."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Sex Discrimination Commissioner Anna Cody said she was sorry Hanson had also experienced domestic violence, with the national crisis affecting one in four women and girls in Australia, but criticised her message.

"Any suggestion that victim-survivors share the blame is harmful, wrong, and dangerous," she said.

"Domestic violence is never the responsibility of the person experiencing it. Just this month, two women and two girls have been allegedly murdered."

Women's Community Shelters chief executive Annabelle Daniel said the evidence was clear that domestic   and family violence is a gendered issue.

"With Australia in the grip of a housing affordability crisis, it's nowhere near as easy as 'just leave'," she said.

"Affordable housing, professional support and community inclusion prevent women becoming homeless because of domestic and family violence in the first place and support their recovery after abuse."

In a Facebook post on Thursday, Hanson said there is a "concerted effort by some in the media to constantly take my comments out of context".

"But some within rival media decided to use only a few quotes and made out that I downplayed domestic violence," she said.

The One Nation leader linked the declining trust in media to recently announced job cuts at Nine newspapers.

"I'm growing less tolerant of many journalists within the [mainstream media] and so too are the public," she said.

Hanson also walked back a number of comments on different issues, including paid parental leave and increasing defence spending to 5 per cent of the nation's economic output.

title.en: 'Literally terrifying': Does this 'rogue' experiment offer a glimpse of our future?
title.zh: “简直可怕”：这个“流氓”实验是否让我们看到了未来？

summary.en: An autonomous AI agent escaped its testing environment and hacked another technology platform during internal capability experiments.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An AI agent powered by OpenAI broke free of its testing environment and hacked a real-life company, in an incident experts said shows the "magnitude" of the cybersecurity threat posed by artificial intelligence.

The incident, announced by the tech company in a statement on its website on Wednesday, saw a combination of OpenAI models launch a cyber attack on a separate tech platform, Hugging Face, during an internal test of OpenAI's capabilities.

Professor Geoff Webb, Australian laureate fellow in the department of data science and artificial intelligence at Monash University, told SBS News it was "literally terrifying" to consider what the same systems could do in the hands of a "malicious actor".

"It shows the magnitude of the task we have in protecting ourselves from these systems in the future," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The news comes after two recent incidents that showed Australia's vulnerability to cyber attacks: when millions of Australians had their data accessed in an Origin Energy hack, and thousands of Australian medical records were accessed in the Partnered Health hack.

Toby Walsh, laureate fellow and professor of artificial intelligence at the University of New South Wales' department of computer science and engineering, said the developments were "troubling".

"All of these models now have pretty strong cyber-capabilities, both for uncovering flaws, bugs that we can then fix, but also in the wrong hands, to exploit those bugs," he told SBS News.

"At the moment, we're relying on the goodwill of OpenAI to tell us what's happening ... We need tougher controls and oversight."

The saga started when Hugging Face, an AI platform for building and sharing machine learning tools, spotted an intrusion from an autonomous AI agent system, writing on their website the attack was "different from anything we had handled before".

OpenAI then announced their models were responsible for the intrusion, after they detected a zero-day flaw in Hugging Face's online security.

"Zero-day flaw means it's a foundational flaw that needs to be fixed now, instantly. You don't wait," Walsh said.

Webb told SBS News the problem with the incident isn't that OpenAI went 'rogue'.

"It wasn't that it decided to do [the attack] anyway. It was told to do it, and it did it. It has now got the capability of figuring it out."

The problem, he said, was that "OpenAI thought they'd put it inside a box it couldn't escape from".

The incident isn't the first to demonstrate the cybersecurity threat of AI. Anthropic temporarily restricted its Claude Mythos model in May after it found more than 10,000 security vulnerabilities in critical software.

Paid practical placements are being rolled out to university students in 10 frontline allied health fields under a major Commonwealth expansion.

From July next year, eligible students will receive up to $338.60 a week, with the program forecast to cost $745 million by the end of the decade.

The payments build on an existing scheme for teaching, nursing, midwifery and social work students introduced just over a year ago.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese used the first day of Labor’s 50th National Conference to announce the new measure, which he said will provide cost of living relief for students and support the future healthcare workforce.

Albanese addressed the conference to outline the expanded payments, make several other announcements, and criticise One Nation.

The prime minister said it is "surprising" such a scheme doesn’t already exist.

"Paid prac is already making a real difference, it’s helping students with the cost of living while they train and that’s why we’re expanding it," he said on Thursday.

"This is an investment in our future healthcare workforce. We need more of them, and this will help more Australians get the qualifications our nation needs."

Hundreds of delegates have converged on Adelaide for the three-day conference, which sets out the party's agenda and policy stances.

Albanese said it was up to Labor to show the difference the government was making to people's lives, rather than just airing grievances.

"People's genuine frustrations deserve a practical response, not just an emotional one," he said.

"You can go a long way in politics, for a long time, by raging against a system that you are part of, without a plan to fix it ... that doesn't build anything."

Albanese stressed the need to tackle long-term challenges as well as deal with daily issues.

"Our focus remains squarely on helping with the cost of living, on the practical measures that matter to people and make a positive difference to their lives," he said.

Albanese also used the speech to hit out at One Nation, which has polled above Labor in some recent voter surveys.

"All those attention-seeking culture wars imported from overseas, all those trips around the world to talk Australia down, cannot disguise the fact that none of them have anything new or anything positive to offer our country," he said.

The prime minister also announced the creation of a Fair Work Court aimed at resolving workplace disputes.

While the 50th Labor conference is not expected to be confrontational, several major policy issues will be on the agenda for debate.

body.en:
Australia's 20 biggest superannuation funds have almost $15 billion invested in gambling-related companies, despite growing concern about the social harm caused by the industry.

A report released on Thursday by the Alliance for Gambling Reform found the sector holds $14.8 billion in gambling stocks.

Australia's largest fund, Australian Super, has the biggest exposure at $4.9 billion — more than double any other fund — while Australian Retirement Trust, Colonial First State, UniSuper and Aware Super round out the top five.

Gambling company Aristocrat Leisure is just one of the companies into which retirement funds are flowing.

Despite many funds having responsible investment policies, approaches to gambling-related risks remain "limited, inconsistent and largely inadequate", according to chief executive of the Alliance for Gambling Reform, Martin Thomas.

He said many Australians would be shocked to learn how much of their money was being invested into the industry.

"There's starting to be a realisation just of how socially damaging gambling is," he told the Australian Associated Press.

Harms from gambling are not consistently treated the same way as harms arising from other industries such as tobacco and alcohol, he said, with the latter routinely screened out of superannuation investments.

Australians are losing more money per capita to gambling than any other country — about $32 billion a year.

A spokesperson for Australian Super said apart from its Socially Aware option, the fund does not apply investment screens to gambling companies.

"We invest to help members achieve their best financial position in retirement," they said.

"We engage with certain ASX-listed companies either directly or with other investors to better understand their initiatives to deliver responsible gaming practices and appropriate governance practices."

Super funds could make more ethical choices about where they put their money, he said, noting gambling investment was a relatively small part of their overall investments, which may range in the hundreds of billions of dollars.

"There is so much opportunity out there for them to do the right thing," he said.

Thomas urged those who were concerned to contact their super fund to find out how much they were investing in gambling.

"We're not looking to ban gambling; we just think it's a harmful legal adult product and should be regulated," he said.

"But we do think it should be shunned by the investment community, particularly super funds, particularly because we're all made to contribute to these super funds."

body.en:

Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) comprise up to 50 per cent of our calories. And while some provide significant nutrients for a balanced diet, others could be responsible for damage in every major bodily organ. So, what are UPFs, and are they as bad as they're made out to be? Watch Insight episode Processed Food Fight on SBS On Demand.

At 39, after a period of feeling very fatigued and getting subsequent testing, Danni Duncan was diagnosed with stage 2 bowel cancer last year.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The Melbourne-based fitness coach then went down a rabbit hole researching contributing factors that can lead to bowel cancer and wondered if the ultra-processed foods (UPFs) she ate growing up could have contributed to the cause.

"Alongside other contributing factors — of course, it's not just the ultra-processed food — one of the common denominators was this big influx of ultra-processed food through the 90s."

While direct causality between UPFs and cancer has not been established, a study based at Massachusetts General Hospital led by Dr Andrew Chan found an association between high consumption of UPFs and an increased risk of having abnormal growths in the bowel, which can lead to cancer.

Danni says she ate a lot of UPFs growing up and that her childhood was "very highly ultra-processed".

"Breakfasts were Coco Pops, Rice Bubbles with sugar on top ... Tiny Teddies, Shapes, chips, Nutella, ham sandwiches on Wonder White bread and McDonald's."

'Ultra-processed' foods (such as confectionary and soft drinks) are products that have been industrially manufactured — containing ingredients such as preservatives and additives that would not be found in the home.

And Australians are among the leading consumers of UPFs, according to Phillip Baker, a public health researcher at The University of Sydney.

"We're eating somewhere between 40 and 50 percent of our calories from ultra-processed foods," Baker said.

Unlike 'processed' foods, UPFs have only been part of our diet for the past 70-80 years.

body.en:
Census night is Tuesday 11 August, and every person in Australia — including Norfolk Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Christmas Island — must be counted.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) conducts a Census of Population and Housing every five years to gather what officials describe as a snapshot of the nation.

It includes up to 66 questions spanning a person's ancestry, religious affiliation, sex recorded at birth and even how they commuted to work that day.

Emily Walter, a Census national spokesperson at the ABS, said many people will be completing the Census for the first time.
